sec: Pituitary feedback, sick-euthyroid and resistance states

items.q: Match the listed pituitary/hypothalamic feedback states to their typical free-hormone / TSH pattern — 1) Primary thyrotoxicosis 2) Sick-euthyroid (printed pattern) 3) Resistance to thyroid hormone (RTH) … A) ↑FT4, ↓TSH B) Normal FT4, normal TSH (printed totals look low) C) Normal/slightly raised FT4 with normal/raised TSH
items.exp: Primary thyrotoxicosis raises free T4/T3 and suppresses TSH; sick-euthyroid as printed leaves totals normal with rT3 high and free T3 low; RTH is associated with normal/raised free hormones and non-suppressed TSH. (Book p903)

items.q: An ICU patient has normal TSH, low total T3 and elevated rT3 one week after admission for sepsis. The most consistent interpretation is:
items.exp: Low T3 with high rT3 in critical illness fits the source's sick-euthyroid sequence; primary hypothyroidism would also raise TSH. (Book p903)

items.q: Assess these sick-euthyroid statements per the source: I T4 is normal in the early phase. II Reverse T3 typically rises because D3 activity dominates.
items.exp: The page prints T4 as normal with T3 low and reverse T3 high early in non-thyroidal illness. (Book p903)

items.q: Which condition is the odd one out among the source's TSH-suppressed (primary thyrotoxicosis) mimics?
items.exp: RTH typically has non-suppressed TSH because the pituitary resists thyroid hormone feedback, unlike primary thyrotoxicosis where TSH is suppressed. (Book p903)

items.q: In sick-euthyroid syndrome, the source lists elevated ___ as the most characteristic biochemical marker.
items.exp: Reverse T3 rises because deiodinase type-3 inactivates T4 to rT3 instead of activating it to T3. (Book p903)

items.q: A patient has persistently non-suppressed TSH with raised free T4 and a normal alpha-subunit / pituitary MRI. The most likely diagnosis is:
items.exp: Non-suppressed TSH with raised free hormone and a normal MRI in a familial setting fits RTH; TSHoma typically raises the alpha-subunit and shows a sellar mass. (Book p903)

items.q: Match the following state to the expected TSH/free-T4 print on the page — 1) Primary thyrotoxicosis 2) Primary hypothyroidism 3) TSHoma 4) Sick-euthyroid early … A) ↑FT4, ↓TSH B) ↓FT4, ↑TSH C) ↑FT4, non-suppressed TSH D) Total T3 ↓, rT3 ↑, TSH normal
items.exp: Primary thyrotoxicosis suppresses TSH; primary hypothyroidism raises TSH; TSHoma gives raised free hormone with non-suppressed TSH; early sick-euthyroid preserves total T4 with low T3 and high rT3. (Book p903)

items.q: Evaluate pituitary feedback: I RTH usually presents with low TSH and high free T4. II Sick-euthyroid syndrome typically produces normal TSH in its early stage.
items.exp: RTH has non-suppressed TSH; sick-euthyroid typically keeps TSH normal early. (Book p903)

items.q: After cardiopulmonary bypass a patient is clinically euthyroid but has total T3 below range, rT3 above range and normal TSH. Which intervention is most consistent with the source?
opts: No replacement — observe and treat the underlying illness
items.exp: Sick-euthyroid changes are adaptive; the source does not recommend routine hormone replacement for ICU patients. (Book p903)

items.q: Which gene is the source's classic association with resistance to thyroid hormone?
items.exp: RTH is most commonly linked to thyroid-hormone receptor β mutations on the page. (Book p903)

items.q: In critical illness, the source's preferred test for diagnosing underlying thyroid disease is ___.
opts: Free T4 (and free T3) rather than total T4
items.exp: Total T4 is misleading because TBG and albumin drop in critical illness; free hormone assays are the page's preferred test. (Book p903)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a state where TSH typically rises (per the source's grouping)?
items.exp: Early sick-euthyroid syndrome keeps TSH normal, whereas primary hypothyroidism, recovery from thyroiditis and iodine deficiency all can elevate TSH. (Book p903)
